title: Davao Prolific guyabano: Fruit and Tree Characteristics
metaTitle: Davao Prolific guyabano: Fruit and Tree Characteristics
metaDescription: Davao Prolific guyabano is a guyabano variety. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best.
excerpt: Davao Prolific is a registered guyabano variety, also sold or known as Davao Prolific soursop or NSIC Ss 01. It was registered with the National Seed Industry Council in 1995 as NSIC 1995 Ss 01. Roberto Coronel bred it. Its record notes a yield of 5 to 8 fruits.

Compare it with the others in our [guyabano variety finder](/crop-varieties), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. items: **Yield:** a recorded yield of 5 to 8 fruits.

blocks.text: Key facts about Davao Prolific guyabano
When does it bear, and how much?

A registered tree variety is described from its mother tree, not from trial plots. The mother tree of Davao Prolific was about 7 years old and about 3 to 4 meters tall when it was registered. Its record notes a yield of 5 to 8 fruits. It bears every year, with fruit in August September. A grafted or marcotted tree bears years sooner than one grown from seed, and its yield climbs as the tree grows.

Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
No pest or disease ratings are published for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.

The pests and diseases that hit guyabano fields most often: [anthracnose](/diseases/anthracnose), [mealybug](/pests/mealybug), [Oriental fruit fly](/pests/oriental-fruit-fly). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.

A fruit of Davao Prolific weighs about 1726.5 grams, and its shape is irregular heart shaped. The flesh is creamy white and soft and spongy. Its sweetness measured 15.4 degrees Brix, the share of sugar in the juice. Most table fruit tastes sweet from about 12 Brix up. The edible part is 82.5 percent of the fruit. Its fruiting season is August September, bearing annual.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Fruit:** Irregular heart shape, about 1.7 kg, light green soft skin, creamy white, soft, spongy flesh, pleasantly sub acid, about 15.4 Brix, about 82 percent edible.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: the first registered guyabano: a short, spreading tree with big, mostly flesh fruit (about 82 percent edible). Check these against what farmers near you have seen, because the same variety can do differently from one town to the next.
Where and when to plant Davao Prolific guyabano

Pick a selection with big, evenly shaped fruit and few seeds. Hand pollination helps fruit set. A registered tree variety is a selection from one proven mother tree, and only grafted, budded or marcotted plants carry its traits. A seedling grown from its seed can turn out quite different. So buy from a nursery accredited by the Bureau of Plant Industry, and ask which mother tree the scions came from. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Pagtatanim ng puno](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-puno).

items: Buy grafted or budded plants from an accredited nursery, with the variety name on the tag.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Plant a few trees first if the variety is new to your area, before you fill the whole farm.
Write down the planting day, inputs and harvest, so you can compare varieties on your own ground. anee.io keeps these records for you.

items.q: Is Davao Prolific soursop the same as Davao Prolific?
items.a: Yes. Davao Prolific soursop is another name for Davao Prolific, registered as NSIC 1995 Ss 01. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.
The record shows a recorded yield of 5 to 8 fruits. Your own yield depends on the soil, water, fertilizer and pests on your farm.

items.q: Where can I buy planting material of Davao Prolific?
items.a: Buy grafted, budded or marcotted trees from a nursery accredited by the Bureau of Plant Industry, so you get the true variety. Ask your provincial agriculture office for the nearest one.
